Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the run-chase! The Indian players are out there in the middle but Harmanpreet Kaur is not on the field. Smriti Mandhana will lead in her absence. Bangladeshi openers, Murshida Khatun and Sharmin Akhter also walk out to the middle now. Meghna Singh to start the proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE …

Bangladesh’s bowling effort was again pretty disciplined but they would feel that they have given away too many runs on this pitch. Marufa Akter was brilliant with the new ball and got the first breakthrough for the home team after which spinners also played a crucial part with some tidy bowling. However, they could not get those wickets in the middle overs which took India’s score over 200 despite five wickets in the last 5 overs. Nahida Akter and Sultana Khatun both took two wickets each but it is upto the batting department of Bangladesh now to step up and clinch a historic series win. Can they do it against the mighty Indians? We shall find out. Stay tuned for the run-chase!

India started their innings on a cautious note but they were soon reduced to 40-2 after Yastika Bhatia was run out in an unfortunate manner while backing up at the non-striker’s end. Smriti Mandhana was looking good but the pressure of dot balls got to her and soon departed in the 22nd over to put more responsibility on Harmanpreet Kaur at the other end. However, she found an able partner in Jemimah Rodrigues and both of them showed great application to keep India’s innings going. Harmanpreet though had to retire hurt in the 37th over after she suffered a painful blow on her left hand. Rodrigues though kept going and found crucial boundaries to up the ante, Deol also batted well and after she departed, Kaur came back to the field. Both of them batted till the 49th over and though India lost a flurry of wickets in the last over, Rodrigues’ 86 and Kaur’s 52 have put them in a strong position.

India have posted a decent score on the board, in fact going by the scores of the last ODI, this seems like a winning total. The pitch is not easy to bat on and India are surely the happier side going into the break.

Nahida Akter performs the chase and cuts it off. She fires an accurate throw to Nigar Sultana at the batting end who catches Rana short of her crease while she was looking to complete the third run. India Women finish with 228 on the board!

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the second ODI to commence as the two umpires make their way out to the middle. Bangladesh Women are seen in a huddle near the ropes before they disperse. Priya Punia and Smriti Mandhana will open the innings for India Women Women. Marufa Akter has the new ball in hand and will start the proceedings for Bangladesh Women Women. Off we go...

Harmanpreet Kaur, the captain of India Women, says that they are not dependent on the toss and they are just looking to play good cricket and back themselves. Adds that they did not play to their strength in the last two games and are looking to do better in this game. Informs that they have two changes - Harleen Deol comes in for Pooja Vastrakar and Bareddy Anusha makes way for Meghna Singh.

Nigar Sultana, the skipper of Bangladesh Women, says that they want to bowl first. Adds that it is a fresh wicket and want to restrict India to a low total. Mentions that they gained confidence from the win in the third T20I. Informs that Shorna Akter is currently under observation, she is replaced by Lata Mondal.

Bangladesh Women (Playing XI) - Nigar Sultana (C) (WK), Nahida Akter, Ritu Moni, Murshida Khatun, Fahima Khatun, Marufa Akter, Fargana Hoque, Lata Mondal (In place of Shorna Akter), Sultana Khatun, Rabeya Khan, Sharmin Akhter.

India Women (Playing XI) - Priya Punia, Smriti Mandhana, Yastika Bhatia (WK), Harmanpreet Kaur (C), Jemimah Rodrigues, Harleen Deol (In place of Pooja Vastrakar), Amanjot Kaur, Deepti Sharma, Devika Vaidya, Sneh Rana, Meghna Singh (In place of Bareddy Anusha).
TOSS - The coin toss lands in the favour of Bangladesh Women and they have opted to BOWL first.

India Women, on the other hand, would be hurting after a shocking defeat in the first game. They are a powerful unit with quality in both batting and bowling department but their execution with the bat has been pretty poor right throughout this Bangladesh tour. It is high time the batters join the party as bowlers continue to put India in good positions with some pretty disciplined performances. Can India Women take the series to the decider? Or Will Bangladesh Women register their first-ever ODI series win over India Women? We shall find out. Toss and team news in a bit.

Bangladesh Women were brilliant with the ball in the first game and that got them to an unlikely win after they were bowled out for 152 while batting first. The star of the show with the ball was Marufa Akter with four wickets but they need to work on their batting to win consistently. Nigar Sultana, the skipper would be a key force in the batting department and expect Bangladesh to leave no stone unturned in their bid to clinch a historic series win.

It is time for the second ODI between Bangladesh Women and India Women after the home team, Bangladesh managed to take the lead in the series with a morale-boosting win against a more fancied Indian team. It was Bangladesh Women’s first ever ODI win over their Indian counterparts and let’s see how things pan out in this second ODI.

It is time for the second ODI of the India Women's tour of Bangladesh. The game will be played at Shere Bangla National Cricket Stadium, Dhaka. India Women will be under pressure as they take on hosts Bangladesh Women. India Women lost the first game by 40 runs under the DLS method creating history by defeating the Asian cricketing giants in India Women. The hosts will look to carry on the confidence and seal the series which would be a monumental moment in the history of Bangladesh Women's cricketing journey. Nigar Sultana and her players will be confident after their maiden win against India Women in the last game. On the other hand, Harmanpreet Kaur will hope for her side to bounce back in this game and level the series. The primary concern for India Women have been the inability to keep ticking the scoreboard against the spinners and they would want to overcome it in this game. Which side will come out on top?
